title: Payer Offset and Recoupment Radar
one_liner: Reconstruct the silent payer clawbacks buried in the 835 provider-level adjustment segment, then dispute the ones that lack notice or exceed state look-back limits.
customer: Community and mid-size hospitals, physician groups and MSOs, and RCM outsourcers who want a recovery line item. SaaS at $1-3k/month, or 15-25% of reversed recoupments.
problem: Payers increasingly claw money back by netting it inside the electronic remittance (835) PLB provider-level balance segment, or by short-paying unrelated claims. These adjustments carry cryptic reason codes and no patient or claim detail. Cash posters drop them into a suspense or 'other adjustment' account, or write them off. The overpayment letters that justify them arrive by mail, fax or random emails and are never matched. Many states cap retroactive recoupment look-back windows and require claim-level notice, but no one checks whether the payer complied.
solution: Ingest 12-24 months of 835s and the payer's overpayment and audit letters (PDF/email/fax OCR). Rebuild every offset to claim level. Flag recoupments with no valid notice, past the state or contract look-back, duplicating a prior recoupment, or hitting claims already appealed. Generate dispute letters and track outcomes. A payer scorecard shows clawback dollars per $1M paid, which gives the CFO leverage at contract renewal.
why_now: Payer payment-integrity programs are scaling with AI-driven post-payment audits and coding-policy downcodes. Medicare Advantage audit pressure is rising. Hospitals staffed thin after the 2025-26 Medicaid and margin squeeze cannot chase each offset by hand. Post-payment recoupment is the fastest-growing part of the denial problem and the least instrumented.
revenue_model: Contingency 15-25% of recoupments reversed, or $1-3k/month per facility for monitoring plus a $5-10k onboarding audit. Payer scorecards can be sold to hospital associations.
non_obvious_insight: Denial management tools watch denied claims. Recoupments are not denied claims. They are negative dollars in the remit file that nobody owns. Only cash posters see them and they are told to just post them. In a typical mid-size hospital these unmatched offsets total mid-six to seven figures a year, and dispute success is highest exactly where the payer skipped required notice. The data is already sitting in files the hospital owns.
first_30_days: Ask 5 friendly hospital and group cash-posting managers for 12 months of 835s (clearinghouses can export them), which requires only a BAA. Write a parser for the PLB segments (about a week of work) and produce a 'recoupment leakage report' showing unmatched offset dollars per payer. Use the number to sign 2 contingency pilots, and build the letter-matching module on real customer data.

title: LOMA Rescue for Newly Flood-Mapped Homeowners
one_liner: Door-to-door service that gets newly mapped flood-zone homeowners an elevation certificate and a FEMA map amendment (LOMA) package before they are forced into flood insurance, with surveyors paying for the leads.
customer: Homeowners whose parcels were just moved into FEMA high-risk zones, who pay $600-900 for an elevation certificate plus filing. Licensed surveyors pay $75-150 per booked job, and private flood MGAs pay referral fees for owners who do not qualify.
problem: Thousands of homes were newly mapped into Special Flood Hazard Areas. Mandatory purchase kicks in fast, and change notification is not mandatory, so many owners learn from a lender letter. Many do not know that a home whose lowest adjacent grade sits above the base flood elevation can petition out. A one-time survey cost competes with a permanent premium annuity plus escrow increases.
solution: A parcel-level tracker of FEMA map-change communities, with screening from public elevation and LiDAR data. We mail and door-hang targeted homeowners with a fixed-price 'get out or get covered' offer. We book a vetted surveyor, file the LOMA package, and route non-qualifiers straight to private flood quotes (referral fee) and mitigation contractors.
why_now: Cotality reports (2026-09-18) that new FEMA maps put thousands of homes into high-risk zones across 100+ communities in 12 states. Homeowners must secure cover within 45 days, and for 10% of homeowners escrow already exceeds principal and interest. NOAA's flood inundation mapping reached nearly 100% of the US population in September 2026, which raises public awareness of flood exposure.
revenue_model: Flat $700-1,000 homeowner package split with the surveyor (about 25-30% margin), plus $50-150 referral fees on private flood or NFIP binds for non-qualifiers. Later sold as a white-label to title companies and community lenders.
non_obvious_insight: The 'uninsurable' problem is here solved by contesting the map, not by finding a carrier. Evidence from https://www.carriermanagement.com/news/2026/09/18/292073.htm: the top newly mapped communities are Escambia County FL (2,344 properties), Pender County NC (678), Chattanooga TN (635), Ithaca NY (428) and Methuen MA (428). The article says change notifications are not mandatory, leaving some homeowners uninformed, and that homeowners have 45 days to secure flood insurance. About 4,500 named parcels in five communities is a concrete addressable list with a hard deadline and no dominant consumer-facing service. Only owners with grade above base flood elevation qualify, so the model needs screening and an honest fallback.
first_30_days: Pull the parcel lists for the five named communities from county GIS and FEMA change notices. Pre-screen elevations with public LiDAR. Sign 2 local licensed surveyors on per-job pricing. Mail 1,000 letters or door hangers in Escambia and Pender with a fixed price and a free eligibility check. Target 20-30 booked certificates in the first month.

title: Landfill Airspace Recovery Contractor
one_liner: Mine old landfill cells to recover airspace, not metals, and sell it to operators at a fraction of the cost of new capacity.
customer: Owners of landfills with under about 10 years of permitted capacity, in airspace-constrained markets: municipal and regional authorities, and independents in the Northeast, Mid-Atlantic and parts of the West.
problem: New landfill cells take years to permit and tipping fees in constrained markets often exceed $100 per ton. Insiders dismiss landfill mining because recovered metals and RDF are low value, so nobody prices the airspace.
solution: An airspace audit (drone LiDAR, borings, waste characterization) followed by a mobile trommel and ballistic-separator spread. It excavates old cells, screens fines for cover and fill, pulls metals and plastics, and re-places compacted residual. Contracts are priced per cubic yard of airspace recovered, compared to the cost of new capacity and haul-out. It skips cells with unknown PFAS risk until sampled.
why_now: Elevated commodity prices, cheaper vision sorting and robotics, tighter EPR and diversion rules that shrink incoming tonnage certainty, and PFAS liability pushing operators to characterize legacy cells anyway.
revenue_model: $25-75K audit fee, then $/CY of airspace recovered (or a share of avoided haul-out cost), plus a share of recovered commodities.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone prices the contents of the landfill. The scarce, regulated, appreciating asset is the airspace, and the true replacement lead time is 10 years.
first_30_days: Screen 20 landfills with under 7 years of remaining capacity using public permit data and satellite volumetrics. Offer free desktop screening and a paid audit of the oldest cell. Lease a trommel by the month rather than buying.

title: Neutral Referee Network for Drone Delivery Noise
one_liner: A $40 Remote-ID-plus-microphone puck network that logs every delivery-drone overflight, becoming the neutral record in neighborhood noise fights.
customer: City planning and council staff in suburbs receiving Amazon Prime Air, Wing or Zipline service, HOAs, plaintiffs' law firms building nuisance or trespass cases, and drone operators that want third-party proof they follow agreed corridors.
problem: Residents count passes by ear (one Richardson, TX resident logged 52 passes on a 'slow day'). The city says it has no authority over routes, and the FAA leaves route management to operators. Operators self-report their own flights, so nobody has authoritative, ground-level, timestamped evidence for complaints, environmental reviews, negotiations or lawsuits.
solution: Small tamper-evident pucks (ESP32 receiving broadcast Remote ID, plus a calibrated MEMS microphone) mounted on homes and utility poles. They log drone ID, operator, altitude, dwell time and dB(A) at the ground. Monthly overflight reports, corridor heat maps and legal-grade evidence packs are produced per neighborhood. It works like airport noise monitoring for a world with no airport.
why_now: Amazon is expanding drone delivery toward roughly 500 US locations by end of 2026, and September 2026 coverage shows resident revolts in Richardson, TX and Michigan suburbs. The FAA's final Part 108 BVLOS rule has been at White House review since July 2026. Remote ID has been mandatory since 2024, so every compliant drone already broadcasts an identity that cheap receivers can log.
revenue_model: Cities: $15k to $40k a year for a 30-to-60-node network plus reports. HOAs: $2k to $5k a year. Evidence packs: $500 to $2,000 each to law firms. Operators: $20k to $60k a year for verified community-compliance dashboards (with published methodology so neutrality is preserved).
non_obvious_insight: Whoever holds the calibrated, tamper-evident log becomes the referee. Cities and residents lack legal control of the sky but hold leverage through evidence in FAA environmental reviews, permits and litigation, and operators will pay for a credible referee to head off regulation.
first_30_days: Build 20 pucks and give them to residents in Richardson and one Michigan suburb. Publish an open weekly dashboard and send it to the local newspaper and council staff. Convert the first paying HOA, city pilot or law firm evidence pack by day 30.

title: Exchange for Shelved Academic Projects and Null Data
one_liner: Buy the 'graveyard' of academic labs, meaning abandoned projects, validated knockout lines, half-built assays and failed-experiment data, and resell them as dossiers with an interview slot to seed biotechs and AI-bio data teams. Supply is anchored by a paid lab-closure clearance service.
customer: Sellers: departing postdocs, PIs downsizing or closing labs, and department chairs and EHS offices who must clear the space. Buyers: seed biotech founders, AI-bio and virtual-cell model companies that need experimental data including null results, pharma target-validation groups, and CROs that need validated cell models. Dossiers sell for $3-30k, and closure concierge fees run $5-15k.
problem: Every lab has a graveyard: KO lines, reporter constructs, a half-optimized assay, a screen that didn't pan out, and boxes in the -80 labeled 'JK 3/14 P3 #2'. When a postdoc leaves or a lab shrinks, the physical items are discarded or become orphaned, and the reasons the project failed leave in the postdoc's head. Meanwhile a startup or AI-bio team pays 12 months and $500k to rebuild the same tools and rediscover the same dead ends. Published literature is heavily biased toward positives, and models trained only on positives are systematically overconfident.
solution: Two-sided wedge. Supply side: 'Lab Closure Concierge' is a fixed-fee triage service for labs that are closing or downsizing. It inventories freezers, plasmids, cell lines and mouse lines, interviews the departing postdoc for 90 minutes to capture provenance and failure reasons (transcribed and structured with AI), disposes of hazardous items compliantly, and flags what is worth keeping. Demand side: a curated catalog of 'dossiers': the physical or digital assets, protocols, raw data including nulls, plus a paid call with the person who built them. Use a standard institutional license or MTA template with a revenue share to the university, so overloaded tech-transfer offices approve it because the alternative is a dumpster.
why_now: NIH grant terminations, indirect-cost fights and uncertain 2026 budgets are pushing labs to shrink or close. Biotech shutdowns have also left surplus bench assets (verify current scale). AI-bio companies are openly short of high-quality experimental data, especially negative data, and pay for it. Tech-transfer offices are understaffed. LLM transcription and structuring turns a 90-minute interview into a searchable dossier cheaply.
revenue_model: Closure-concierge flat fee paid by the department or PI. A 25-30% commission on dossier sales, with revenue share to seller and institution. Annual data-subscription tier for AI-bio buyers (curated null-result feeds).
non_obvious_insight: The vials are worth very little. The value is provenance plus the 'why it failed' story stored in one person's memory, and it evaporates the day the postdoc's visa or contract ends. So the product is not a marketplace for samples, it is structured exit-knowledge capture with a physical-asset appendix. Because the university owns the IP anyway, the clean structure is to make the institution a paid party rather than an obstacle.
first_30_days: Use your own postdoc network to line up 3-5 labs that are shrinking or have departing postdocs. Offer a free triage-and-catalog audit in exchange for permission to list a few assets. Produce 10 dossiers with structured interviews. Cold-email 30 seed biotechs and AI-bio data leads with the top 5 dossiers. Close one sale at $3-8k. Use that transaction to test the university revenue-share template with one tech-transfer office.

title: Robot-Training Disassembly Lab for E-Scrap Magnets
one_liner: A small teardown shop where displaced office workers are paid to take apart hard drives and servers on camera, so sales of robot-training data cover the labor that makes rare-earth magnet recovery uneconomic.
customer: Two paying buyers. (1) Physical-AI and robotics labs that need real contact-rich manipulation data. (2) Rare-earth processors and ITAD firms that want magnets and boards already pulled out of steel and PCB streams. The workers are laid-off office staff and underemployed recent grads.
problem: The circular-materials brief says the rare-earth bottleneck is collection and disassembly, not chemistry, and that pulling magnets from hard drives often costs more than the magnets are worth. Robotics labs are short of messy, real-world demonstration data. Meanwhile the expert-gig data economy (Mercor and similar) pays only for screen work, contractors complain of falling pay, and recent-grad underemployment is 42%.
solution: Rent a bay near an ITAD or data-center decommissioner and take in drives and servers that are already sanitized under NIST 800-88. Workers wear head cameras and instrumented gloves or tool sensors and follow step protocols. An annotation pipeline labels screw types, connectors and failure cases. Sell the licensed video and force data by the annotated hour. Sell the pre-extracted magnet fractions, aluminum and boards to processors. Later, the same corpus trains a disassembly arm that lowers labor cost. Workers earn wages plus a skills log.
why_now: Physical-AI funding and data hunger are at a peak in 2026. DoD and DOE are subsidizing domestic rare-earth supply, and hyperscalers are pushing processors to recover magnets. DRAM prices are up about 400% since early 2024, and data centers turn hardware over every 12-18 months, so teardown yield keeps rising. White-collar hiring is frozen for the young (Stanford: 22-25-year-olds in AI-exposed jobs are 19% below trend).
revenue_model: Data licensing per annotated hour (hypothesis to test: $35-60/hr, versus roughly $25-28/hr loaded labor). Materials sales of magnets, aluminum, boards and DRAM/SSD. Per-unit processing fees from ITAD partners. Later, licensing the teardown protocols and a robot-ready dataset.
non_obvious_insight: Disassembly looks unprofitable only because we value just the recovered material. The task has a second output, training data, that has no recovery-cost floor. The uglier and more variable the end-of-life product, the more out-of-distribution and valuable the data is to robotics labs. Recycling's mess is the data moat, and the displaced labor is the cheap input.
first_30_days: Sign one ITAD or decommissioner for a free lot of about 500 sanitized drives. Sign one robotics team for a paid 100-hour pilot. Recruit six workers from laid-off tech and helpdesk groups. Build three capture stations (camera plus glove rig, about $1.5K each). Sell the first magnet and aluminum lot to a local processor to prove the unit economics.

title: Earn-In Equity for Journeymen Buying Trade Shops
one_liner: A platform that turns a retiring HVAC, plumbing or electrical owner and a 25-year-old journeyman into a multi-year vesting buyout with a pre-agreed valuation formula, seller note and SBA-ready paperwork.
customer: Retiring owners of 5-40 employee trade shops (sellers pay) and licensed journeymen or foremen aged 22-35 (buyers), plus SBA lenders that fund the final tranche.
problem: Most trade-business owners plan to retire within years, yet only about half have a succession plan. Selling to private-equity roll-ups strips the local shop, and employees cannot get $1M+ loans with personal guarantees or clear the licensing hurdles. Owners hesitate to leave, and buyers lack a track record that lenders trust.
solution: An 'earn-in': the journeyman converts part of pay, bonus and sweat into equity tranches at a formula price (a multiple of trailing owner earnings with a collar), while the owner keeps a seller note and consulting role. The platform supplies valuation, legal documents, state-by-state license-qualifier planning, a data room from job and dispatch software, and a lender packet. After three to five years it supports the final SBA-financed buyout, monitoring callbacks and margins as an early-warning system.
why_now: An estimated 6 million small-business ownership transitions and up to $5T of enterprise value are expected by 2035, and Gen Z interest in trades and acquisition is rising. Lenders want buyers with operating history, which a staged earn-in builds. Field-service software now produces clean data to underwrite from.
revenue_model: A seller-paid setup fee of $4-$8k, a 1% fee on closed value plus lender referral, and a SaaS charge of $99-$299 per month for tracking tranches and KPIs. Later, a small gap-capital fund.
non_obvious_insight: The successor is already inside the business, and the bottleneck is trust and time, not capital. A formula-based earn-in makes 'when and at what price' knowable on day one, lets owners retire on a schedule, and lets buyers learn to run the shop before taking on debt. It also preserves local reputation better than a roll-up.
first_30_days: Recruit five retiring owners through local supply houses and trade associations. Charge $2,500 for a pilot 'succession blueprint' plus legal docs. Interview 20 journeymen through trade schools and union halls. Partner with an M&A attorney and one SBA lender. Aim for three signed earn-ins by month six.

title: Bonded US-Only Remote Operators for Robots
one_liner: A staffing company for physical AI: background-checked, bonded, US-resident remote operators working from secure facilities on SLA-backed shifts to assist robotaxis, delivery robots and teleoperated humanoids.
customer: AV fleets, sidewalk and delivery robot operators, humanoid and mobile-manipulation startups (Series A to C) and the enterprise or health customers who demand US-based, vetted humans. The buyer is the head of operations or safety.
problem: Autonomy plateaus at 99%, and the last 1% is human labor. Waymo disclosed at a February 2026 Senate hearing that some remote assistance staff are in the Philippines, drawing political heat (Sen. Markey called it a safety issue). 1X's Neo puts a remote operator with a VR headset inside customers' homes, which is the central privacy objection. Robot startups have no staffing operation for 24/7 shift coverage, vetting, training, security controls and quality scoring.
solution: Secure operator centers (not homes) staffed with vetted US-resident operators drawn from gamers, drone pilots, veterans and military spouses. Certification per partner interface, quality scoring, audit trails and a 'named operator and session log' feature so a homeowner or hospital can see who touched what. Start with teleoperation for data collection and pilot demos, then move into live remote assistance and compliance packs.
why_now: Consumer humanoids and expanding robotaxi fleets (Waymo alone is at about 500k paid rides a week across 14 cities) make operator-hours a rapidly scaling cost. The Senate scrutiny of offshore remote assistance and the Neo privacy debate mean a 'US-only, vetted, auditable' premium is about to be demanded by regulators and enterprise buyers.
revenue_model: Billed operator-hours at $40-70/hour against a loaded cost of $25-30/hour. Premiums for compliance, security clearance and named-operator features. Setup fees for integration and certification.
non_obvious_insight: Every 10,000 robots create thousands of operator jobs, and the political fight will be about where those people sit, just as with call centers. Whoever builds the trusted, audited labor pool early owns a compliance premium that AI labs cannot easily build in-house.
first_30_days: Rent a 10-seat secured room in a mid-cost city. Buy Quest headsets and a leader-follower arm set. Recruit 15 operators from gaming and RC-drone communities and pass them through background checks. Offer 100 pilot-hours at cost-plus to 10 humanoid and delivery-robot startups who need demo and data collection help.

title: Group-Block Attrition and Force Majeure Claims Desk
one_liner: A 48-hour, outcome-priced desk that tells meeting and wedding planners whether the 2026 shocks let them escape or shrink hotel attrition penalties, and files the notices on time.
customer: Association and corporate meeting planners without in-house counsel (100-1,000 attendees), destination-wedding planners, DMCs, and youth-sports or choir tour operators holding hotel room blocks.
problem: Hormuz closure (2 Mar 2026), jet-fuel-driven capacity cuts and fare hikes, and UAE hospitality disruption mean groups cannot fill contracted blocks, while booking lead times shrank from 37.5 to 33 days. Attrition clauses often penalize around 20% shortfalls, and force-majeure wording and notice deadlines, not the law, decide outcomes. Small planners miss the 7-30 day notice windows and pay in full.
solution: Upload the contract for a clause map covering the attrition table, cure and mitigation duties, force-majeure triggers, and deadlines. The desk generates the notice letters, sends deadline alerts, and provides a negotiation script and a walk-away vs renegotiate calculator. A partner hospitality lawyer handles escalations at a fixed fee. Cases where the hotel resold freed rooms at higher rates argue mitigation, not force majeure.
why_now: The 2026 disruption produced a wave of disputes between now and winter events. Europe summer ADR rose 4-6% and Turkey flights rose 25% as trips rerouted. In those markets hotels can resell freed blocks at higher prices, which weakens their damages claims.
revenue_model: $390 flat for the clause map and deadline pack, about 15% of penalties avoided as a success fee, and fixed-fee lawyer escalations. An annual $1,200 deadline-tracker subscription is aimed at DMCs.
non_obvious_insight: The strongest argument is often mitigation, not force majeure. In rerouting hot spots the hotel resells rooms at higher rates and cannot claim losses it did not suffer. The moat is a dataset of clause wording and outcomes, plus never missing a deadline.
first_30_days: Recruit 20 planners from association-executive and wedding-planner forums with a free 'contract triage' of one block. Have one hospitality lawyer review the template letters. Convert the first 5 to paid flat-fee packs and log every outcome to build the clause database.

title: Subsurface Desert Mapping From Free Radar Satellites
one_liner: Use open L-band radar data to map buried channels and structures beneath arid ground for mineral and water explorers.
customer: Junior critical-mineral explorers, uranium and lithium prospectors, groundwater drillers, national geological surveys and arid-region water utilities.
problem: Exploration in deserts costs a fortune per drill hole, targeting is often guesswork, and airborne geophysics is expensive. Explorers need cheaper first-pass targeting.
solution: Combine weekly-repeat NISAR L-band radar (open data), Sentinel-1 and, outside North America and Europe, ESA Biomass P-band to map buried paleo-channels, faults and shallow structure in hyper-arid terrain. Deliver target packages per license block, plus a success-fee option.
why_now: NISAR launched in July 2025 with an open-data policy, and ESA's Biomass P-band radar launched in April 2025. Demand for critical minerals is at a peak. Radar penetration only works in very dry ground, so scope is narrow but valuable.
revenue_model: $20-60k per license block. Success fee or royalty on discoveries. Annual subscriptions for geological surveys.
non_obvious_insight: Seeing beneath sand from orbit sounds like science fiction, and it is now possible with free data. The business is expertise and interpretation, not satellites.
first_30_days: Pick two well-studied arid areas as proof cases and reproduce known buried channels. Show results to 20 junior explorers with licenses in arid regions. Sell the first two block packages at a discount for case studies.

title: File-Cabinet-to-Pipeline Digitization Crew
one_liner: A mobile scan-and-extract crew that turns a newly acquired trades company's filing cabinets and paper job files into a clean customer and equipment-age database plus a ready-to-run replacement and membership campaign.
customer: Acquirers of legacy HVAC, plumbing, roofing, pest, electrical and garage-door companies (search funders, holdcos, PE add-on platforms). The buyer pays a fixed fee plus a share of revenue from jobs sold off the output. Brokers are a secondary channel, using it as sell-side data-room prep.
problem: Acquired trades firms often run on paper, desk phones and old PCs, so the owner cannot see permit errors, warranty problems or job margins. Any AI, field-service software or roll-up integration needs structured data first. Meanwhile decades of installs sit in file drawers as an unused equipment-age database.
solution: A two-person crew with document scanners and phone capture spends 5-10 days on site. Vision-model extraction pulls customer, address, equipment make/model/serial, install date, service history, warranty status and membership status. Output is import-ready for ServiceTitan, Jobber, Housecall Pro and QuickBooks, plus an 'asset-age' list: homes with systems older than a set threshold, expiring warranties, lapsed maintenance customers and contract renewals. It includes a letter/SMS campaign and prepaid-membership offer templates, with job tagging so results are measured.
why_now: Handwriting and form extraction from photos became accurate and cheap in 2025-2026. Bain's 2026 GP outlook says 39% of GPs expect no material financial impact from AI on portfolio companies this year, and Bain's midyear report says leaders redesign workflows rather than layering tools on top. Both point to data readiness as the gap. First-time buyers of small trades firms are more numerous than ever, and each faces the same digitization backlog.
revenue_model: $8-15K fixed fee per business, plus 8-10% of first-year revenue from jobs tagged to campaigns generated from the output. Sell-side version for brokers: $3-5K data-room prep before listing.
non_obvious_insight: What looks like clutter is a proprietary, geocoded equipment-age database of thousands of households, the highest-intent lead list in the trades, and the buyer paid for it in the purchase price without knowing. Rob Brooks found '30,000 customer records' in filing cabinets, 13-year-old computers and desk phones, could not see permit or warranty problems until he digitized, and reached $1.3M EBITDA from $340K SDE in 14 months with about 800 customers prepaying three years of membership (https://www.acquiringminds.co/articles/rob-brooks-gary-air). Winsor Fireform's buyers spent seven months digitizing roughly 90% paper records (https://acquiringminds.co/articles/andrew-sova-alex-clark-winsor-fireform-novo-foundry). Tew & Taylor ran on Excel and mailed checks, creating a large receivables backlog (https://www.acquiringminds.co/articles/jack-rauch-tew-taylor). Bain's GP outlook notes 39% of GPs see no material AI impact on portfolios in 2026 (https://www.bain.com/insights/private-equitys-reality-check-gp-outlook-2026/). Every buyer solved digitization ad hoc, and none treated the archive as revenue.
first_30_days: Pick HVAC in one metro. Find 3 recent small-business buyers through ETA communities and brokers, and offer one a near-cost pilot. Scan and extract 2,000 records in 3 days, mail letters or SMS to the oldest-equipment homes, and count booked calls per 500 contacts. Publish the result as a case study, then price the service at $8-15K plus revenue share. Meanwhile approach 5 HVAC business brokers with the sell-side data-room version.

title: Toddler Talk: Voice-Based Developmental Screening
one_liner: A phone-recorded three-minute parent-child talk sample plus automated screening workflow that helps pediatric practices catch speech and developmental delays earlier and capture reimbursement.
customer: Pediatric practices and health systems (developmental screening is billable under CPT 96110), Early Intervention programs and Medicaid managed care plans.
problem: Speech-language delay is a very common developmental issue, but screening relies on parent questionnaires with modest sensitivity, practices under-screen and Early Intervention waitlists are long. Kids are referred late.
solution: Phase 1 (no diagnostic claims) is a text-based well-visit screening workflow that increases completion and billing capture and collects consented audio. Phase 2 adds speech models that estimate vocabulary diversity, word combinations and turn-taking latency, giving clinicians a triage report. Phase 3 is a validated FDA pathway.
why_now: Speech models now handle child speech far better than before. Developmental screening is a CMS Child Core Set quality measure (from memory), so Medicaid plans pay for completion. Multimodal models make sample-based scoring feasible.
revenue_model: Per-screen fee or per-provider subscription ($200-500 a month), plus quality-improvement contracts with Medicaid plans, and later a per-report fee.
non_obvious_insight: Parents already record toddlers constantly. The bottleneck is not detection technology but screening completion and triage, so the winning move is to attach to the reimbursed screening code and Medicaid quality measures first and upgrade the signal later.
first_30_days: Partner with 2 independent pediatric practices through a developmental-behavioral pediatrician advisor. Run a 60-day free text-intake screening pilot. Capture consented audio for retrospective validation. Pitch one Medicaid plan's quality team on completion-rate lift.

title: Collections That Hunt the Payer, Not the Patient
one_liner: A contingency-fee receivables firm for ambulance agencies and ER physician groups that, within 30 days of a self-pay bill, screens the patient for retroactive Medicaid eligibility and files the application for them, turning accounts debt buyers would take at 2-4 cents into full Medicaid payments.
customer: County and municipal EMS agencies, their outsourced ambulance-billing companies, and independent ER, anesthesia and radiology physician groups in Medicaid-expansion states. Rural hospitals under 100 beds are the second wave.
problem: Self-pay accounts sit through 90-180 days of statements before they go to an agency or get sold to a debt buyer, and buyers pay only pennies (a few cents on the dollar for medical accounts). Most states let Medicaid reach back only about 3 months before the application date, so by the time a normal collections workflow gives up, the window in which a real payer could have been found has already closed. Patients get dunned for money they may never have owed, and the provider recovers almost nothing.
solution: Take a nightly feed of new self-pay accounts (demographics only, under a BAA). Screen each one for likely Medicaid or charity-care eligibility. Contact the patient in the first two weeks with a simple offer: we complete your Medicaid application for free. Then file the application, chase documents and caseworkers, and bill Medicaid retroactively for the provider. Patients who do not qualify are routed to charity care or a payment plan, and nobody is ever dunned. The firm is paid a contingency on Medicaid dollars actually collected. The dashboard shows each account's days left in the retro window, so providers see the clock that traditional collections ignore.
why_now: The 2025 budget law (OBBBA) cuts Medicaid retroactive coverage to 1 month for expansion adults and 2 months for everyone else, for applications from January 2027. From then on every day of delay burns covered dates, so speed to application becomes the whole product. Providers are also under revenue pressure, states keep passing medical-debt limits that make selling accounts harder, and Medicaid redetermination and work-requirement churn in 2027 makes eligibility-navigation skills scarce and valuable.
revenue_model: 15-20% contingency on Medicaid reimbursements recovered, with an optional $1-2k/month platform fee for charity-care and medical-debt compliance reporting. Ambulance and physician-group accounts are small ($800-$2,500 each) but high in volume and nearly free to service once the screening flow is built.
non_obvious_insight: Collections looks like a persuasion business but is really a timing business. Every step of the traditional workflow (statements, calls, placement at day 120 or later) pushes action past the point where a third-party payer can still be found. Run the workflow backwards, find the payer inside 30 days, and you get the rare collections company that patients thank you for and that pays the provider 10-30x what a debt buyer would.
first_30_days: Pick one expansion state with a 3-month retro window. Hire two ex-hospital eligibility reps and one engineer. Offer 3 county EMS agencies or their billing companies a free back-test of the last 12 months of self-pay accounts, showing how many were eligible and inside a window where enrollment would have paid. Convert the best result into a contingency pilot on new accounts, ideally with an existing certified navigator status. First Medicaid approvals typically land 45-90 days after filing, so signed pilots come in month 1 and cash in months 3-4.

title: Medicaid Work-Rule Retention Packets for Health Plans
one_liner: A pay-per-retained-member service that assembles the income-proxy, exemption and medical-frailty evidence packets Medicaid expansion enrollees need to keep coverage, sold to the health plans and clinics that lose revenue when members are dropped.
customer: Medicaid managed-care plans (especially regional and provider-sponsored plans in expansion states), FQHC networks, and hospital systems with large expansion panels. Secondary buyers: state agencies and counties that have said they will not add staff.
problem: Work requirements start January 1, 2027 in 44 states. CMS projects 2.3M people lose Medicaid in 2027, and 55% of enrollees are unaware of the rule. States are scraping existing data. Nebraska hired no new staff, and its medical-frailty code list omitted certain cancers, heart failure and HIV. North Carolina bars self-attestation and requires 3 months of records. About 25% of Dare County's expansion enrollees are self-employed. County Medicaid units have ~10% vacancy and staff with only 11-13 months' experience. A KFF-cited expert calls hours tracking 'a problem no state has solved at scale.'
solution: Consent-based enrollee flow, started via text or QR code at a clinic or from a plan's outreach. The enrollee links bank, gig-platform, payroll or 1099 data through open-banking and income-verification connectors. The system computes monthly income against the $580 threshold (80 hours x $7.25) that satisfies the rule, with seasonal averaging where the state allows. It then generates a state-formatted verification submission. In parallel it mines the plan's or clinic's claims and EHR history to match the medically frail categories and produces clinician attestation forms. It tracks the 30-day grace window and 6-month redeterminations. Volunteer-hour and school verification come from partner organizations. A human navigator queue handles exceptions.
why_now: CMS issued its interim final rule June 1, 2026 and a medical-frailty implementation deck on September 8. Nebraska (May 1) and Montana (July 1) are live, so real failure modes are visible. States may request extra information from enrollees in year one, and exemption self-attestation is allowed only once before 2028, so documentation becomes mandatory after that. The January deadline sets hard budget urgency.
revenue_model: Per-packet fee plus per-member-per-month retention fee paid by the plan or clinic. Assumption to validate: a retained expansion member is worth hundreds of dollars per month in capitation, so $30-100 per retained member is easily justified. Optional state contracts priced per verification.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce input is evidence for people the state cannot see in wage data (self-employed, gig, seasonal), not caseworker capacity. Health plans and clinics, not states, have both the financial incentive and the claims data to prove frailty. The federal income equivalent ($580/month) turns an impossible hours-tracking problem into a cash-flow calculation. Evidence: NC counties describe the informal-economy documentation gap, 10% vacancy, no self-attestation and 3 months of records (https://www.northcarolinahealthnews.org/2026/04/30/medicaid-work-county-challenges/). Nebraska confirmed the ~$580 income option and said it will not hire or add staff (https://www.kff.org/medicaid/a-closer-look-at-nebraska-the-first-state-planning-to-implement-a-medicaid-work-requirement/), and its frailty code list had gaps (https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/nebraska-medicaid-work-requirements-launch-first-state/818992/). CMS projects 2.3M coverage losses in 2027 (https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/cms-medicaid-work-requirements-final-rule-state-guidance/821631/). State staffing gaps: https://kffhealthnews.org/medicaid/medicaid-cuts-work-requirements-state-staff-shortages/. Risk: 26 states are suing over the rule.
first_30_days: Offer free pilots to 1-2 FQHCs in Nebraska or Montana, where enrollees already face the requirement. Build on an open-banking connector and an income-verification API. Draft the income-proxy calculator and a frailty-evidence template from CMS's September deck. Book meetings with member-retention leads at 5 regional Medicaid plans, with a paid pilot targeted for the November-December pre-January enrollment wave. Get a HIPAA BAA and consent language in place first.

title: Coolant Assay Lab for Liquid-Cooled GPU Racks
one_liner: Oil analysis for GPU clusters: mail-in and inline coolant testing that catches corrosion and biofilm before they kill racks, and produces the neutral evidence for warranty fights.
customer: Neoclouds, colocation operators and enterprise AI teams running 1-50 MW with direct-to-chip liquid cooling. Insurers and lenders are second-wave buyers.
problem: Rack densities past 100 kW make liquid loops mandatory, and hundreds of small operators are running them for the first time. Their expertise is IT, not fluid chemistry. Glycol degradation, galvanic corrosion, dissolved copper and biofilm clog cold-plate microchannels and cause slow thermal throttling or sudden leaks. When a failure happens, the rack OEM, CDU vendor, coolant supplier and colo each blame the others and nobody has data.
solution: Sample kits and an inline sample-port sensor puck for every coolant distribution unit loop. A partnered industrial fluids lab runs standard assays: inhibitor level, pH, conductivity, particle count, bacteria, and metals. The software trends each loop and flags drift. A chain-of-custody Coolant Passport records every sample. Add dispatch of a flush-and-refill crew when a loop fails a threshold.
why_now: Next-generation rack systems shipping in 2026 assume liquid cooling by default, and operators are retrofitting halls that were never plumbed for it. The wave of first-time operators is happening now, before standards exist.
revenue_model: $400-1,200 per loop per quarter for assay and trending. $3-10k per emergency flush dispatch. Later, data licensing to insurers and OEMs for warranty and underwriting.
non_obvious_insight: The failures will come from boring chemistry, not from chips. Whoever holds the longitudinal sample history holds the evidence in every warranty dispute, and becomes the de facto standard, the way engine oil labs did for fleets and aviation.
first_30_days: Partner with an existing industrial fluids lab in Texas or Virginia that runs ASTM methods. Offer three small neoclouds a free first assay in exchange for read access to their thermal telemetry. Publish a short field guide on loop failure modes. Convert those three to a paid quarterly plan.

title: Buyer-Side RFP Claim Verifier for Cities
one_liner: Automated reference-checking and claim-testing for the flood of AI-polished bids that city procurement offices cannot separate.
customer: Procurement offices at cities, counties, school districts and cooperative purchasing bodies with lean staff, plus state procurement agencies.
problem: Governments use GenAI to write RFPs and vendors use AI to answer them, so every response looks perfect. Dallas County is cutting IT staff. Only 5.3% of AI-related contract provisions address transparency, and local tech contracts average 7 years. A bad pick locks the city in.
solution: Ingest bids, extract every checkable claim (reference customers, uptime, certifications, incident history, prior contracts) and verify against public records, contract databases, court dockets, security advisories and automated outreach to references. Deliver a one-page evidence-scored comparison that the evaluation committee can attach to the award file.
why_now: The vendor-side tools (NationGraph raised $22.5M to help vendors read documents and write proposals) have collapsed the signal in bids. Michigan's fraud-system disaster ($20M settlement plus $78M replacement) has made buyers nervous.
revenue_model: $1.5-5K per RFP for small buyers, or annual subscription for a state or co-op ($25-100K). A per-audit fee for high-risk software and AI awards.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone is selling to the vendor who is writing. The scarce, budgeted, blame-averse buyer is the one drowning in identical documents and has no tool that raises the cost of lying.
first_30_days: Take five closed public RFPs and publish a teardown showing which claims failed verification. Offer free pre-award checks to 5 county procurement offices. Charge from the second use.

title: Data Centers Fund Their Host Utility's Leak Repairs
one_liner: A turnkey program where a data-center developer pays to cut real water losses in the host utility's own system and gets a signed, metered, same-source volume to show regulators and neighbors.
customer: Data-center developers and colo operators fighting permit resistance (Cheyenne, Ohio, New York, Texas), plus the small and mid-size host utilities that receive the repairs. The developer pays.
problem: Insiders think 'water positive' means wetland or agricultural offsets in some other watershed. Locals and regulators now want physical relief on the same source in the same year. Meanwhile many small utilities lose 20-30% of what they treat, and can't fund repairs.
solution: Run an AWWA-style water audit of the host utility. Rank repairs by gallons saved per dollar (main breaks, service leaks, failed valves and meters). Fund local crews and verify the savings with district-metered-area flow data. Deliver a signed 'verified gallons saved' report to both the utility and the permitting file. The utility gets capacity to serve the new load without new supply.
why_now: Texas is making data-center non-reporting a crime and a bar to permits. Ohio scrapped its general discharge permit after more than 7,000 comments, New York has a moratorium, and Cheyenne revoked a permit. Australia's planned standards explicitly cover funding extra water infrastructure. Developers need mitigation that neighbors can verify.
revenue_model: 10-15% program-management fee on repair spend, margin on crew contracts, and a performance bonus per verified 1,000 gallons saved. A $15-25k paid feasibility study is the door-opener.
non_obvious_insight: The cheapest same-source gallon is one the utility already treated and lost. This turns the data center from the utility's rival for water into its capital source, and 'water positive' gets judged by neighbors and permitting boards, not by sustainability reports.
first_30_days: Use public loss-audit filings (Texas, Georgia and California require them, in my understanding) to rank utilities near contested or pending data-center projects by real losses per connection. Write a 10-page 'loss-to-offset' report on three of them. Send it to the developers, and to the utilities as a free mailer. Aim for one paid feasibility study within 30 days.

title: Cask Audit: Proof of Existence for Whisky Investors
one_liner: An independent inspection, gauging and valuation service that verifies investor-owned whisky casks exist, contain what was sold, and are worth what the seller says.
customer: Retail cask investors, IFAs and wealth managers, insolvency practitioners and law firms, and honest cask brokers who want a trust seal.
problem: The cask market has been in a glut since 2022 (auction surplus, distillery consolidation, lower price per litre) and has documented fraud cases where audits found casks missing or filled with substandard spirit. Investors cannot verify holdings or exit.
solution: Field inspectors in bonded warehouses attest existence, fill level, strength, cask type and warehouse-receipt ownership, with geotagged photos. Quarterly valuations use bottling yield and market comps, and brokers pay to join an 'audited cask' registry.
why_now: In a downturn demand shifts from buying more to proving what you own. Fraud taints every honest broker, so third-party proof is worth paying for.
revenue_model: GBP 150-300 per cask audit, broker subscriptions for continuous audit, and valuation reports.
non_obvious_insight: Bonded-warehouse access is already a contractual owner right, so inspectors are cheap to deploy, while buyers of proof are motivated by loss and by seller reputation. The bourbon cask market is a later expansion. Confirm warehouse cooperation and local regulation early.
first_30_days: Recruit 2 warehouse-keepers, audit 30 casks for 10 investors at a GBP 100 pilot rate, publish anonymized findings, and approach IFAs and insolvency firms.

title: Repatriation-of-Remains Concierge for Immigrant Families
one_liner: A fixed-price service that gets a loved one's body home across borders, and later a low-cost membership that pre-funds it.
customer: Immigrant families on one corridor at a time (for example US to Mexico or Central America, the Philippines, India or Nigeria), plus consulates, churches, mosques, community associations and funeral homes without international skills.
problem: Sending remains home costs thousands (often $5-15K, unverified) and requires consular paperwork, health permits, embalming, sealed caskets, air cargo rules and destination-side logistics. Families use GoFundMe, church collections and opaque middlemen, in days, while grieving.
solution: Intake in the family's language, document assembly (consulate forms, permits), a vetted network of embalmers, cargo forwarders and destination funeral homes, insurance and payment plans, and one coordinator. Later add a $8-$15/month repatriation membership underwritten through a licensed insurer partner.
why_now: Community payment and remittance rails are digital, translation and document assembly are cheap with AI, and immigrant communities are large and trust-network driven. Funeral homes treat this as an add-on they don't understand.
revenue_model: 15-25% service margin on $6-12K cases, membership fees, and insurer commissions.
non_obvious_insight: The mainstream industry treats repatriation as a sideline, but for these families it is the primary product. Corridor-specific know-how is the moat, and trust travels through churches and consulates.
first_30_days: Choose one corridor and one metro. Partner with a funeral home that already does it. Sign 3 churches or a consulate liaison. Run 5 cases at cost to document the exact process and price it.

title: Payroll and Tax-Prep Rails for Scholarship Credit
one_liner: Embeddable 'route my credit' flows in payroll, CPA and banking tools that turn the federal scholarship tax credit into a mass-market donation default.
customer: Scholarship-granting organizations (SGOs) that need small donors and pay per gift; distribution partners such as payroll platforms, PEOs, credit unions and CPA firms take a revenue share.
problem: The credit (capped at $1,700 per donor) starts in 2027 and 31 states have opted in. Estimates run $25-50B a year, but 40% of adults have not heard of it and Treasury rules are still under White House review. Many SGOs are brand new and know how to court large donors, not tens of millions of ordinary taxpayers.
solution: A white-label widget and API: check state eligibility, choose an SGO, set up a one-tap payroll deduction or card gift, auto-generate the receipt for tax filing, track pledges and send reminders. SGOs get a dashboard of pledges and cost per donor. Launch with CPA year-end planning and one payroll or PEO partner.
why_now: The credit starts in 2027, and payroll elections and year-end tax planning in Q4 2026 are the first place defaults get set. Rules are unresolved, so a compliant routing layer gets designed into workflows now.
revenue_model: 2-4% of routed gifts paid by SGOs, or a flat per-donor fee, plus revenue share to payroll and CPA partners.
non_obvious_insight: Because the credit offsets tax owed, the barrier is not generosity but awareness and friction. Whoever owns the default placement where tax decisions happen, in payroll elections and CPA offices, captures the flow, much as workplace-giving platforms did for charity.
first_30_days: Sign 2-3 SGOs in an opted-in state, including one new community-foundation SGO. Build a one-page pledge flow and a receipt generator. Approach 20 CPAs and one small payroll or PEO provider. Run a Q4 pledge drive built as pledge now, fulfill in 2027, and stay flexible until final Treasury rules.

title: Buffet Lab: Hotel Breakfast Lines as Test Market
one_liner: Paid two-week trials that put reformulated or novel ingredients on real hotel and cruise breakfast lines, with item-level consumption, waste and hot-hold colour data.
customer: Food manufacturers facing the FDA petroleum-dye phase-out, and makers of natural colours and alternative proteins such as fermentation whey, rubisco and purple-sweet-potato colour, including farmer-owned processors. Hotels and cruise operators are the supply side.
problem: Dye reformulation costs $50K-$500K per SKU and takes 12-24+ months, and Walmart private label goes dye-free in January 2027. Whey is short and alt-protein funding has collapsed, so startups need cheap real-world proof. Lab sensory panels and retail test markets are slow, expensive and blind to failure modes like colour fade under lights, texture after hot-hold, and portion rejection by the roughly 12% of Americans on GLP-1s.
solution: Recruit 30-50 independent hotels plus one cruise or resort operator. Supply product free and track item-level consumption against control, plate waste, restock rates by daypart, QR feedback, hot-hold time and light exposure, with colorimeter photos of colour drift. Optionally A/B half-portions. Deliver a two-week acceptance, waste and stability report, and sell recurring access to the panel to CPG innovation teams.
why_now: The FDA dye phase-out targets December 2027, with 22 states adding food-restriction rules and a federal ultra-processed food definition in review. Whey concentrate is up 108% in two years, alt-protein funding fell to $881M in 2025 with only $197M in H1 2026, and GLP-1 users are reshaping portions and protein preferences. Buyers want supply-risk answers, not sustainability stories.
revenue_model: $12K-$30K per product trial. Hotels receive product, about $40/day and waste analytics. Panel subscriptions for CPG innovation teams of $60K-$120K/yr.
non_obvious_insight: A hotel breakfast line is the largest measurable eating experiment in commerce: repeat business travellers, captive choice, fixed hot-hold time and lighting, and a natural weigh-back at clearing. It stress-tests exactly the things that kill natural-colour and protein reformulations, much faster than a retail test market.
first_30_days: Recruit 8 independent hotels via an owners' association and approach 5 natural-colour and ingredient startups directly. Run one paid pilot, for example a dye-free pastry glaze or cereal, at about $8K to prove the report format.

title: Insurability-at-Close Escrow for Home Listings
one_liner: Listing agents pre-underwrite a house and price the cheapest retrofit fix before listing, so buyers stop discounting for 'uninsurable' uncertainty.
customer: Listing agents, brokerages and sellers in Florida, California and Colorado foothill markets, paying a fee at closing.
problem: Contracts collapse or reprice when buyers cannot get a bindable quote inside the contract window. Homes labeled uninsurable trade to cash buyers at a discount. Much of that discount is uncertainty about fixable issues (roof age, vents, tree clearance), not permanent risk.
solution: A pre-listing 'Insurability File'. Run 3-5 carrier and E&S quotes through a partner agency, then identify the 1-3 cheapest fixes and get contractor quotes. Hold the retrofit cost in escrow at close and give buyers a bindable-quote certificate valid through closing. The buyer gets certainty and the seller gets a closing.
why_now: Citizens has shrunk from about 936K to about 395K policies, so private binding is possible for many Florida homes again. Fannie and Freddie now accept ACV roof coverage (Mar 2026), which opens cheaper insurable paths. Colorado and California rules now credit mitigation.
revenue_model: $750-1,500 per listing at close, plus a 15-25% referral margin on retrofit work and placement commission through the partner agency.
non_obvious_insight: The 'uninsurable' discount is a mispriced-uncertainty premium, and certainty can be bought. Whoever holds the bindable quotes at listing time sets the price.
first_30_days: Pilot with 3 top-producing agents in one Colorado or Florida market. Take 10 stuck or repriced listings, build files by hand, and measure price recovery against comps. Then productize the file template.

title: Protein Cartridges for Heavy Rare-Earth Polishing
one_liner: Skid-mounted cartridges of engineered lanmodulin-type proteins that separate heavy rare earths (Dy, Tb) from magnet-recycling leachate without long solvent-extraction chains.
customer: Magnet recyclers and small separators whose processes end in mixed rare-earth concentrates, plus DoD- and DOE-backed pilot programs.
problem: Recovery projects often end with mixed concentrates that still need separation, which conventionally takes hundreds of solvent-extraction stages that China dominates. Heavy rare earths are the acute chokepoint after China's 2025 export controls.
solution: Protein-based sorbents (naturally lanthanide-binding proteins, studied at Penn State and Lawrence Livermore) engineered for heavy-RE selectivity. They are packed in modular columns as a polishing step at ambient conditions. The business model is cartridge consumables plus skid rental.
why_now: Heavy rare earths are now a stated national-security bottleneck, DOE announced $134M for demonstrations in June 2026, and AI protein design has made engineering selectivity a computation problem instead of a decade-long screen.
revenue_model: Consumable cartridge sales plus skid lease. Early revenue from SBIR grants and paid pilots.
non_obvious_insight: Rare-earth chemistry fights in a sea of near-identical ions, while proteins evolved to tell lanthanides apart. The hard part is now designing the scaffold, not discovering the effect.
first_30_days: License or partner with a university lab. Run bench tests on real recycler leachate. Apply to DOE and DoD SBIR programs. Sign 2 recyclers to paid pilots.

title: Adaptive Paper: Kumon Economics, AI Back Office
one_liner: Weekly personalized paper practice packets sequenced from phone photos of last week's handwritten work: adaptivity with no screen and no chatbot in the child's hands.
customer: Homeschool and hybrid families (parent pays; ESA/scholarship-eligible later), microschools, Catholic and independent schools, and eventually districts in AI-pause cities.
problem: 61% of teachers want less device use, NYC and LAUSD paused AI, and proctored math performance is sliding while screen-based practice looks better. Adaptive practice has lived on screens where AI can do it for the child. Kumon proves parents pay roughly $100-150 a month for paper mastery, but it is rigid and franchise-priced.
solution: A parent photographs the completed worksheet. The back office reads the handwriting, classifies error types (graphing and hand-drawn work are hard to outsource to AI), and prints or mails the next week's 5-day packet with a one-page parent guide. The student never touches a screen or chatbot. Start with math grades 3-8.
why_now: Handwritten-math recognition from phone photos only recently became reliable and cheap. Screen fatigue and AI bans are mainstream. ESA and scholarship-credit money arrives in 2027, and homeschool ESA families want low-cost vendors.
revenue_model: $15-25 per child per month for print-and-mail, $8 for PDF-only. School licenses of $6 per student per month. ESA-vendor listing to capture ESA dollars.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone equates personalization with screens, but the personalization is in the sequencing, and sequencing can happen off-screen once handwriting is machine-readable. Paper is the AI-proof delivery channel and screens are the liability.
first_30_days: Recruit 40 homeschool families through co-op groups with a $9 first month. Run one grade band of math. Have a retired teacher audit the sequencing weekly. Use a print-on-demand vendor. Measure with a short proctored pre/post check so you have outcome data to sell schools.

title: Solar Battery Warranty-Claim Recovery Desk
one_liner: Pool failed-battery claims from small African installers and enforce them against Chinese manufacturers for a share of recovered value.
customer: Solar installers and importers in Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana and South Africa holding failed batteries and inverters.
problem: Africa has imported more battery dollars than panels from China since 2024. Cheap packs fail, and claims need serial verification, BMS logs, RMA logistics and language skills, so installers absorb the losses.
solution: A claims desk that captures failure evidence by QR and app, files with OEMs, consolidates returns and tracks credit notes. The wedge is five Lagos importers with a backlog of dead units.
why_now: The battery import surge of 2024-26 is now reaching failure age, and installer margins are compressing.
revenue_model: 15-25% of recovered value, moving to SaaS plus failure-data sales to insurers.
non_obvious_insight: A warranty is worth only what you can enforce. Batching many small buyers gives leverage over OEMs and produces failure data that insurers need.
first_30_days: Collect backlog lists from three importers and file the first 100 claims.
